  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the maamar with the date and occasion of the second day of Shavuos 5729.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B”H.</t>
    <t s="1">The second day of the festival of Shavuos,</t>
    <t s="2">the year 5729 (1969).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the apparent redundancy of the word "leimor" in the verse, and introduces two interpretations regarding the innovation of the Giving of the Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">“And Elokim spoke all these words, saying,”</t>
    <t s="1">And the precise point is known</t>
    <t s="2">regarding what is written “saying,”</t>
    <t s="3">that since all of Israel</t>
    <t s="4">(the souls of all generations)</t>
    <t s="5">were present at Mount Sinai and heard the Ten Commandments from the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself,</t>
    <t s="6">what is the meaning of “saying”?</t>
    <t s="7">It means “to say to others.”</t>
    <t s="8">And the point of the explanation in this is,</t>
    <t s="9">that through this the verse explains the innovation of the Giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="10">For seemingly, even before the Giving of the Torah they studied the entire Torah</t>
    <t s="11">[as is also understood from the fact that Avraham Avinu fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given,</t>
    <t s="12">for in order to fulfill the Torah one must study it,</t>
    <t s="13">and certainly</t>
    <t s="14">Avraham taught the entire Torah to his son Yitzchak, and Yitzchak taught it to Yaakov and his sons],</t>
    <t s="15">and what is the innovation of the Giving of the Torah?</t>
    <t s="16">And the verse explains,</t>
    <t s="17">that the innovation of “And Elokim spoke all these words” at the Giving of the Torah is,</t>
    <t s="18">that through this the power was given to each and every Jew of all generations,</t>
    <t s="19">that his study of Torah should be in a manner of “saying.”</t>
    <t s="20">And there are two explanations in this.</t>
    <t s="21">That through his study of Torah he causes the Holy One, blessed be He, to speak these words,</t>
    <t s="22">for whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,</t>
    <t s="23">according to which the explanation of “saying”</t>
    <t s="24">(“to say to others”)</t>
    <t s="25">is,</t>
    <t s="26">that the person who studies Torah says to the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="27">as it were, that He should repeat his words.</t>
    <t s="28">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="29">that a person’s study of Torah should be in a manner of “saying,”</t>
    <t s="30">to repeat the words that the Holy One, blessed be He, says,</t>
    <t s="31">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="32">“May my tongue answer Your word,”</t>
    <t s="33">that the words of Torah that a person says are “Your word,” and “my tongue answers” like one who answers after the reader.</t>
    <t s="34">And there is another explanation of “And [He] spoke… saying,”</t>
    <t s="35">that “And Elokim spoke all these words,”</t>
    <t s="36">the Ten Commandments which are the general principles of the entire Torah,</t>
    <t s="37">is “saying,”</t>
    <t s="38">that the Ten Commandments</t>
    <t s="39">(Torah that is above the world)</t>
    <t s="40">should be drawn down into the Ten Utterances through which</t>
    <t s="41">the world was created.</t>
    <t s="42">And likewise is it in a person’s study of Torah,</t>
    <t s="43">that it is in a manner of “And [He] spoke… saying,”</t>
    <t s="44">that from his Torah speech an “utterance” is made,</t>
    <t s="45">the drawing down of influence below.</t>
    <t s="46">And one must understand the connection and relevance of all the above matters in “saying.”</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section cites the Mitteler Rebbe's maamar and the Midrash, explaining that the voice at Sinai was tailored to each individual's capacity, including the physical body.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, in the maamar of the Mitteler Rebbe beginning with this verse, which was said one hundred years ago,</t>
    <t s="2">(after the precise point that the word “leimor” seems superfluous),</t>
    <t s="3">he brings what is stated in the Yalkut,</t>
    <t s="4">“When the Holy One, blessed be He, was speaking, each Jew would say, ‘The speech speaks with me,’ as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="5">‘I am the L‑rd your G‑d’ in the singular.”</t>
    <t s="6">And he explains,</t>
    <t s="7">that this is what is stated in the Midrash</t>
    <t s="8">on the verse “I am the L‑rd your G‑d,”</t>
    <t s="9">that the voice they heard at the Ten Commandments was according to the capacity of each individual,</t>
    <t s="10">the youths according to their capacity, the elders according to their capacity, and the children according to their capacity.</t>
    <t s="11">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="12">that from the reasons for this that he also brings from the statement of the Midrash,</t>
    <t s="13">it is,</t>
    <t s="14">that through this it is understood that the matter of “the speech speaks with me”</t>
    <t s="15">(to each one individually)</t>
    <t s="16">is not only in regard to the soul but also in regard to the body,</t>
    <t s="17">for the distinction of youths, elders, and children is from the aspect of the body.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
